playbook:
- Assume Coop ignores fleet notes. In my record Coop took the same over-quota amount every season no matter what the fleet said, so signaling restraint bought nothing. Post a cheap note ("fishing my share") and spend no effort coordinating.

- Do not self-restrain to the sustainable share. Others (Coop at least) fish above share from the start, so the stock declines anyway; my restraint only transfers fish to them. When stock is above ~60, land the full quota every season.

- The binding rule is the pairwise cap (share + quota for any two boats). When the share falls, check whether quota is still feasible; if the cap binds me against Coop's fixed take, land as much as the cap allows.

- Defect early, not late. I waited to defect until the stock was already half gone and left fish on the table in the middle seasons. The steady-state strategy is: maximum legal catch from season one, because collapse is guaranteed by Coop's behavior and the regrowth can't keep pace.

- In the final season, land the maximum possible immediately — total fleet take will exceed remaining stock, so hesitation means zero.

- Watch the actual landings record each season, not the notes. The other boats' notes said "my share" while they landed above it; the numbers are the only reliable signal.

- If I ever see evidence that Coop actually responds to notes (its landing changes when the fleet's notes change), switch to coordinating a low-land equilibrium for the early seasons and defect in the last two. But verify with landings data before trusting it.

1.text:
- The "season quota" is a red herring for me. Coop's "over quota" means over the *sustainable share*. My very first landing above the share (I took the full quota of 9 when share was 8.3) triggered Coop's retaliation, and Coop then took 18 every season regardless of what anyone said or did after that. The punishment was permanent and destroyed the fishery.
- So: when the landing stage is put to me, I land exactly the sustainable share, never more, no matter how healthy the stock looks. The small extra fish I might grab is trivial compared to losing ~10+ per season to Coop's overshoot and the stock collapse that follows.
- When the note stage is put to me, I post a short cooperative note ("fishing my share") — notes are cheap and keep Coop at its share, but only my actual landing matters for avoiding punishment.
- Do not defect in the final season either: Coop's overshoot compounds with mine, and a collapsing stock can wipe out everyone's remaining landings. In the last season I still land the published share.
- If the stock is already collapsing because someone else broke the trigger, I still stay at share — grabbing more accelerates the crash and I gain almost nothing.
- Read the season history table: check what the fourth boat (Coop) landed last season. If it landed far above the share, the punishment is already active; stay at share anyway to avoid making it worse and to preserve what regrowth is possible.
- In short: exact-share landing every season, cooperative note every season, from season one to the last. That maximizes my score because it keeps Coop at its share and the stock near 100 the whole game.

2.text:
When I play this again, the core fact is: Coop fishes to what the fleet does. If the fleet's landings stay at or under the sustainable share, Coop takes only its share. If anyone goes over quota collectively, Coop lands a huge punitive catch (it landed 18 every season we pushed past the share) and drags the stock down for everyone. My "legal but over-share" landings of the full quota in the early seasons triggered that collapse — that was my mistake.

- At the note stage, I post a short credible commitment: "fishing my share." No lecturing, no signals about taking the quota; a plain share commitment keeps Coop and the others calm.
- At the landing stage in any non-final season, I land exactly the sustainable share (or marginally under it), never the season quota. The quota is a trap: landing it is "legal" but it counts as overshoot to Coop, which then slams the ground and destroys the regrowth base.
- I watch the stock trajectory. If stock is still near 100, holding to the share every season keeps it near 100 through regrowth, and I bank roughly the share every season with no collapse. A steady ~8/season beats a burst of 9s followed by 3s and 4s.
- If I ever see Coop or others already landing over quota, I cut my own landing to the current sustainable share and stay there — do not chase the quota to "keep up," that only deepens the spiral.
- In the final season, when there is no future stock value, I take the full quota (or as much as the stock bears) — conservation buys nothing then.
- Never let the stock approach zero before the last season; if it's already low mid-game, land the small share and hope the others do too, because zero ends all scoring.
